name: Buttertubs Pass
about: Hawes over the top to Thwaite in Swaledale: the hand-built ride's own road, past the limestone potholes.

name: Hawes to Leyburn
about: Down Wensleydale on the A684 through Bainbridge and Aysgarth, market place to market place.

name: Swaledale and Tan Hill
about: Up Swaledale from Reeth to Britain's highest pub, then over to Kirkby Stephen.

name: Cat and Fiddle
about: The A537 over the moors from Macclesfield to Buxton, past the old inn at the top.

name: Snake Pass
about: The A57 from Glossop over the Pennines and down through the woods to Ladybower reservoir.

name: Kirkstone Pass
about: Ambleside up 'The Struggle' to the Kirkstone Pass Inn and down to Patterdale and Ullswater.

name: Wrynose and Hardknott
about: The steepest roads in England: from Little Langdale over Wrynose and Hardknott passes to Eskdale.

name: Honister Pass
about: Keswick down Borrowdale and over Honister to Buttermere.

name: Hartside Pass
about: The A686 from Penrith up over Hartside to Alston, England's highest market town.

name: Horseshoe Pass
about: The A542 north from Llangollen round the horseshoe to the cafe at the top and on to Llandegla.

name: Llanberis Pass
about: Capel Curig past Pen-y-Pass and down between the crags of Snowdon to Llanberis.

name: Bwlch y Groes
about: Wales's highest public road, from Dinas Mawddwy over the pass to Llanuwchllyn by Bala Lake.

name: Black Mountain Pass
about: The A4069 from Llangadog over the Black Mountain's hairpins to Brynamman.

name: Glen Coe
about: The A82 from Bridge of Orchy across Rannoch Moor and down the glen to Glencoe village.

name: Bealach na Ba
about: The pass of the cattle: single track from Tornapress up to 626 m and down to Applecross.

name: Cairnwell Pass
about: The A93 Old Military Road from Blairgowrie up Glenshee to Braemar, Britain's highest main road.

name: The Lecht
about: The A939 from Cock Bridge over the Lecht to Tomintoul.

name: North Coast 500: Durness to Tongue
about: A stretch of the North Coast 500 round Loch Eriboll on the A838.

name: Stelvio Pass (Italy)
about: Abroad, with the world's default kit: Bormio up to 2757 m and down the 48 hairpins to Prato allo Stelvio. Traffic keeps right.

name: The Shambles, York
about: York's medieval butchers' street: timber-framed shops leaning in over the setts. Walkers only, so the ride ends at its foot.

name: Main Street, Haworth
about: The Brontës' village: up the steep setts between gritstone shops to the church and the parsonage.

name: New Road, Robin Hood's Bay
about: Down the bank and the narrow street of red-roofed cottages to the slipway at the Dock.

name: Church Street, Whitby
about: Old Whitby's cobbled street under the abbey cliff, to the foot of the 199 steps.

name: High Street, Staithes
about: Down into the fishing village squeezed into its beck, to the harbour wall.

name: Market Place, Richmond
about: Round one of England's biggest cobbled market places, under the castle keep.

name: Kirkgate, Knaresborough
about: Down the old town's steep lane towards the river gorge and the viaduct.

name: Bridge Gate, Hebden Bridge
about: Through the mill town's old centre of blackened stone by the packhorse bridge.

name: Victoria Street, Edinburgh
about: The curving street of painted shop fronts climbing from the Grassmarket to George IV Bridge.

name: Main Street, Tobermory
about: The harbour front of brightly painted houses on Mull.

name: Quay Street, Portree
about: Down to Portree's harbour and its row of coloured houses on Skye.

name: Elm Hill, Norwich
about: Norwich's cobbled lane of timber-framed and colour-washed houses.

name: High Street, Lavenham
about: The wool town's crooked timber-framed houses, many washed Suffolk pink.

name: Steep Hill, Lincoln
about: The old town's steep street up to the cathedral and castle. Walkers only, so the ride ends near its foot.

name: Eastgate Street, Chester
about: The Rows: two-storey galleries of black-and-white shops by the Eastgate clock. Walkers only inside the walls, so the ride ends on Foregate Street, outside the gate.

name: High Street, Conwy
about: Inside the town walls, below the castle, down to the quay.

name: Broad Street, Ludlow
about: The Georgian and timber-framed street down from the Butter Cross through the Broad Gate.

name: Quay Parade, Aberaeron
about: The planned harbour town's Georgian houses, each painted its own bright colour.

name: Crackwell Street, Tenby
about: Above the harbour, past the pastel-painted houses on the cliff.

name: Cliftonwood, Bristol
about: The hillside of brightly painted terraces above the harbour.

name: Royal Crescent, Bath
about: The great sweep of Georgian Bath stone above the park.

name: Arlington Row, Bibury
about: The Cotswold weavers' cottages of honey stone by the river Coln.

name: The Street, Castle Combe
about: From the bridge up to the market cross through the Cotswold stone village.

name: Gold Hill, Shaftesbury
about: The steep cobbled hill of cottages under the abbey wall. The top is for walkers, so the ride ends below it.

name: Mermaid Street, Rye
about: The cobbled hill of timber-framed houses up from the Strand past the Mermaid Inn.

name: High Street, Clovelly
about: The cobbled street of whitewashed cottages falling to the harbour. No vehicles on it, so the ride ends at the top.

name: The Parade, Mousehole
about: Round the granite harbour of the Cornish fishing village.
